subject: RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()

messages.author: 52c2b686b48e3db4
messages.subject: RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()
parts:
Hi--

I'd be interested in making the output of optimizing() consistent with the output of stan()/sampling(). I left a comment on Bob's feature request with my thinking so far (https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/41), which is that it might make sense for optimizing() to output a 'stanfit' object (but with a different attribute value for the sampler).

But I'd really like to hear what others think the right approach would be.

Bob mentioned that you're hoping to do a major refactor on the command parts of Stan, RStan, and PyStan, so people might want to wait on this until after that. So if this is something it makes sense for me to help with but not until later, that's fine too. (It also seems like maybe a small enough thing that if anyone is in that bit of the code while refactoring something, they might naturally get this done as part of something else. That'd be a good outcome too!)

Since this is my first note to stan-dev, I also wanted to say that I appreciate all the work you're doing, and hopefully it'll make sense for me to help out somehow at some point (whether with this or something else).

Thanks!
David

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()
parts:
Thanks. 

I do not think it is an inconsistency issue.  I would not expect the results from Bayesian sampling to be consistent with a point estimate.  In addition, stanfit is a bit complicated now as it needs to deal with failure of sampling, test gradient, multiple chains, etc.  So it needs a lot of if, else if, ..., else and makes it harder to maintain.  However, it is enough to put the result for a point estimate in a list.  If not, I would rather put it in a object different than stanfit, say a new class called stanoptim.  

Just my opinion of keeping it simpler.

Jiqiang

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()
parts:
[Caveat: I do not use R or RStan but...]

I agree that overloading stanfit seems like it may not be the way forward.  We're talking about making the deterministic optimization available in Stan more featured in the future.  For instance, returning things like local normal approximations to compute uncertainties.  This is not really something that seems nice to shoe-horn into a stanfit object.

Maybe the question to ask is, what features of a stanfit object are you missing when using the optimizer?

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 52c2b686b48e3db4
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()
parts:
Sorry, it seems like 'inconsistent' was confusing. I was just talking about what you do to manipulate the objects, not the actual results. 

Marcus-- In my case, I just wanted convenient access to the parameters like you get with 'extract'  for stanfit objects.  The vector they come in now is a pain to work with, especially with non-scalar parameters. https://groups.google.com/forum/m/#!topic/stan-users/KpQBrQaoEd0

Then when I looked at the list of methods for stanfit objects it seemed like most of them made sense for the output of optimization as well.  That's what made me wonder if they should be the same class. But I can see different classes making more sense. 
David

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] RStan--making output of optimizing() consistent with output of stan()
parts:
I agree with Marcus that it'd be better to have a different
class in R for the output of optimization. I know it's common in
R, but I really dislike overloading objects so that they sometimes
give you one thing and sometimes another based on state.

If something like that gets designed and implemented, it shouldn't
be a problem to make it forward-compatible with whatever changes
we make on the C++ side.

- Bob
